subject.title: fix(agents): re-expose toolsAllow core tools in embedded runs

question: Should finite embedded-run toolsAllow be allowed to re-expose explicitly requested core shell/file tools through restrictive config allowlists, or should those runs fail closed when the configured allowlist removed the requested tool?
rationale: This is a command/file-access boundary: the PR intentionally widens per-run tool visibility relative to configured allowlists, and the linked issue already has security/product-review signals.

options.title: Allow exact re-exposure under existing gates
options.body: Port this PR's shape to current main and require proof that only requested known core tools are restored and deny/sandbox/subagent/provider gates still block them.

options.title: Fail closed instead
options.body: Keep config allowlists as hard caps and add a pre-dispatch blocked/error outcome when a finite toolsAllow requests a tool that cannot be materialized.

options.title: Close in favor of a broader cron/Codex fix
options.body: If maintainers want the broader false-green cron and Codex app-server shape to own this work, pause or close this branch once a viable replacement PR is chosen.

recommendation.title: Allow exact re-exposure under existing gates
recommendation.body: Port this PR's shape to current main and require proof that only requested known core tools are restored and deny/sandbox/subagent/provider gates still block them.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work made the current capability-profile and embedded-runner tool-policy paths the active owner boundary for this decision.
